name: Street Design Qualities in Tianjin: Five Pairwise Perceptions
description:
Method replication: same task, questions and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (98 Baidu street views re-fetched in central and suburban Tianjin, each stitched from four directions: front, right, back, left). Participants compare pairs of places on five design qualities ("Which place has a better enclosure / human scale / complexity / imageability?", "Which place looks safer?"), each with a short definition, 8 pairs per quality.

Original study: Zhou, Ji, Zhang, Wu, Li & Zhang (2025), ISPRS Int. J. Geo-Inf. 14(10), 391. 45 master's-level urban design researchers made 4,321 pairwise choices on 300 stitched Baidu SVIs sampled across Tianjin's six central and four suburban districts; TrueSkill scores (0–1) trained a model that predicted perceptions for 74,000 more images, used in a geographical XGBoost housing price model.

Differences from the original study: (1) images are newly fetched Baidu views, not the 300 original SVIs; (2) a fixed 8 pairs per quality (40 in all) instead of free-length sessions on the authors' platform; (3) the definition wording is ours, as the paper gives only "a clear qualitative definition"; (4) the safety question is worded "Which place looks safer?"; (5) two background questions were added.
author: Zhou, Ji, Zhang, Wu, Li & Zhang

elements.name: consent
elements.title: I agree to take part. My answers are recorded anonymously for research.

elements.name: enclosure
elements.title: Which place has a better enclosure?
elements.description: Enclosure: how well the street feels defined like an outdoor room by buildings, walls, trees and other vertical elements.

elements.name: human_scale
elements.title: Which place has a better human scale?
elements.description: Human scale: how well the size, texture and detail of the physical elements match the size and walking speed of people.

elements.name: complexity
elements.title: Which place has a better complexity?
elements.description: Complexity: the visual richness of a place, how many different buildings, colours, materials, signs and activities there are to look at.

elements.name: imageability
elements.title: Which place has a better imageability?
elements.description: Imageability: how distinct and memorable a place is, so that it stands out and is easy to recognise and remember.

elements.name: safety
elements.title: Which place looks safer?
elements.description: Safety: how safe you would feel walking here.

choices.text: Urban design / planning researcher or graduate student

elements.name: know_tianjin
elements.title: How well do you know Tianjin?

choices.text: I live or have lived there
